messages:
karen (finapp): Hey team — since yesterday our prod traffic to Redwood is getting 500s and massive tail latency. We traced it and it looks like calls are being routed to eu-central-1. Our services are in us-west-2 and we never changed anything. Can you help?

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this, Karen. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces it and a sample request id/response headers if you have one?

karen (finapp): Repro: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat` — response headers show `x-redwood-region: eu-central-1` and `x-request-id: r-9b4c2`. Latency from our app ~1.5s, expected ~120ms.

maria (support): Thanks. Chris / Samir are you able to look at routing? Behavior sounds like source IP-based geo routing picking the wrong region.

samir (networking): Quick hypothesis: customer's egress is hairpinned through a corporate forward proxy/NAT that SNATs to an ISP/colocation IP that GeoIP maps to EU. If Redwood routes by egress IP -> region, that explains it. Karen — can you confirm whether your on-prem egress goes via a corporate proxy or central NAT?

karen (finapp): Yes — traffic goes through our corp forward proxy (squid) then out through our ISP's NAT. We also recently changed the proxy to run in HA behind a load balancer. Didn't think it would affect routing.

chris (eng-infra): Got it. I pulled the backend logs for `r-9b4c2`: backend sees source IP 91.201.45.18 which we currently map to eu-central-1. We also have `region-detection: source-ip` on routing rules for low-latency auto route. That matches Samir's theory.

maria (support): Karen, two possible immediate workarounds: 1) Pass explicit region hint header to pin to us-west-2: `-H \"x-redwood-region: us-west-2\"` (temporary). 2) Use token-scoped routing: create a dedicated token that forces us-west-2 (we can issue from our side) — want us to generate one?

karen (finapp): Workaround 1 helped for a quick test — pinned calls now 120ms. But we need permanent fix.

samir (networking): Permanent fixes: a) Have your proxy preserve original client IP via PROXY protocol / X-Forwarded-For so egress NAT shows the actual internal client IP to downstream — but note many corporate NATs will still SNAT to ISP IP, so b) better is to request your ISP to allocate dedicated egress IPs (static) for us-west egress, or c) add the SNATed egress IP(s) to our account-level egress mapping so we treat them as us-west. Option c is easiest from our side.

chris (eng-infra): To move forward we need: a list of public egress IPs (the SNAT IPs) or a CIDR range, and a contact for a short maintenance window if we need to add to routing tables. Also sending packet captures showing flows helps. Example tcpdump snippet to run on your gateway: 
```
sudo tcpdump -n host api.redwood.com and port 443 -c 5 -w /tmp/redwood-egress.pcap
```
Then share pcap (or a few lines of `sudo tcpdump -n -c 20 host api.redwood.com and port 443 -q`).

karen (finapp): I attached the tcpdump extract and our two egress IPs: 91.201.45.18, 91.201.45.19. Also included proxy config — the proxy does not forward PROXY protocol to the internet-facing LB.

maria (support): Thanks — attaching to internal routing ticket (SUP-9874). I asked infra to add those IPs to Karen's account egress mapping. Samir / Chris: can you confirm if adding these will cause any rollout or cache invalidation?

samir (networking): Adding static egress IPs to account mapping is low-risk. We'll add both IPs to the us-west-2 mapping for Karen's org and update routing cache. TTL of mapping is 60s; after propagation new connections should route correctly. I will schedule a config push now.

chris (eng-infra): Pushed mapping for account finapp -> egress ips [91.201.45.18/32, 91.201.45.19/32] -> us-west-2. Confirming routes invalidated.

deploy-bot: config-push SUP-9874 succeeded in 22s (change: add egress mapping for org finapp).

maria (support): Karen — can you verify now?

karen (finapp): Verified in staging and prod — calls now go to us-west-2, latency back to normal. No 500s. Thank you.

maria (support): Great. Followups we recommend: - Ask your infra team or ISP to allocate a stable egress IP block for us to map (prevents future surprises). - If possible, enable X-Forwarded-For or PROXY protocol end-to-end so you can preserve client origin. - If you need, we can provision a token pinned to us-west-2 as a backup.

samir (networking): Note for internal docs: we should include guidance for customers with central proxies that GeoIP can misclassify SNAT IPs; offer egress mapping as a supported remediation. I'll add a KB.

maria (support): Closing this thread unless Karen wants more. :white_check_mark:

karen (finapp): All good, closing from our side. Thanks everyone! :pray:
